title: Inside a Vec<i32>
subtitle: Push, pop and shrink, and watch the heap buffer

captions.initial: Vec::new() does not allocate: capacity is 0 and the pointer is a dangling, well-aligned placeholder. The first push allocates.
captions.push: len < capacity, so the value is written into spare space: no allocation, O(1).
captions.pushRealloc: The buffer was full. The Vec allocated a new buffer of capacity {new} (was {old}), moved {bytes} bytes into it and freed the old one. Doubling keeps push amortized O(1).
captions.pop: pop returns Some(value) and decrements len. Capacity is kept for future pushes.
captions.popEmpty: The Vec is empty: pop returns None. No exception, no undefined.
captions.shrink: shrink_to_fit reallocated to exactly len elements, giving {saved} bytes back to the allocator.
captions.shrinkNoop: Capacity already equals length, nothing to shrink.
captions.shrinkFree: With len == 0, shrinking frees the buffer entirely and the Vec is back to its non-allocating state.
captions.clear: clear drops every element and sets len to 0, but keeps the allocation: refilling it costs no reallocation.
captions.full: This demo stops at {max} elements, but a real Vec keeps doubling until memory runs out.
captions.firstAlloc: The first push allocates a buffer for 4 elements (16 bytes): a minimum capacity that avoids reallocating for tiny vectors.
